question: If \( \vec{u} = \vec{a} - \vec{b} \), \( \vec{v} = \vec{a} + \vec{b} \) and \( |\vec{a}| = |\vec{b}| = 2 \), then \( |\vec{u} \times \vec{v}| \) is
working: (a-b)x(a+b)=2(a x b), so |u x v|=2|a||b|sin(t)=2*sqrt(|a|^2|b|^2-(a.b)^2)=2*sqrt(16-(a.b)^2). Numeric check with 3 random pairs of length-2 vectors matched option A exactly (e.g. 7.059439).

question: The value of \( \lambda \) so that the vectors \( \vec{a} = 2\hat{i} - \hat{j} + \hat{k} \), \( \vec{b} = \hat{i} + 2\hat{j} - 3\hat{k} \) and \( \vec{c} = 3\hat{i} + \lambda \hat{j} + 5\hat{k} \) are coplanar is
working: Coplanar iff scalar triple product = 0: det[[2,-1,1],[1,2,-3],[3,L,5]] = 7L+28; sympy solve gives L=-4.

question: The angle between two lines whose direction cosines satisfy the equations \( l + m + n = 0 \) and \( l^2 = m^2 + n^2 \) is
working: l+m+n=0 with l^2=m^2+n^2 and sum of squares 1 gives l=+-1/sqrt2 and mn=0; the two distinct lines are (1/sqrt2,-1/sqrt2,0) and (1/sqrt2,0,-1/sqrt2), cos = 1/2 so angle = pi/3 (sympy enumeration confirmed cos 0.5).

question: If \( \alpha, \beta \) and \( \gamma \) are the direction cosines of a line in space, then the value of \( \sin^2\alpha + \sin^2\beta + \sin^2\gamma \) is
working: alpha,beta,gamma are the direction angles with cos^2 sum = 1, so sin^2 sum = 3 - 1 = 2.

question: The foot of the perpendicular from \( (2, 4, -1) \) to the line \( x + 5 = \dfrac{1}{4}(y + 3) = -\dfrac{1}{9}(z - 6) \) is
working: Line: (t-5, 4t-3, 6-9t), direction (1,4,-9). Perpendicularity of (P-Q) to the direction gives 98-98t=0, t=1, foot (-4,1,-3).

question: The shortest distance between the lines \( \dfrac{x}{2} = \dfrac{y}{2} = \dfrac{z}{4} \) and \( \dfrac{x-4}{-2} = \dfrac{y-4}{8} = \dfrac{z-5}{5} \) lies in the interval
The distance between \( (2, 1, 0) \) and \( 2x + y + 2z + 5 = 0 \) is
The function \(f(x)=\dfrac{1}{2-\cos 3x}\), \(x\in\left[0,\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right]\) is

options.label: C
options.text: one to one as well as onto

options.label: D
options.text: neither one to one nor onto

working: f'(x) = -3sin3x/(2-cos3x)^2 < 0 on (0,pi/3), so f is strictly decreasing hence one-one; its range is [1/3,1] (sampled 1.0 -> 0.3333), so with the default codomain R it is not onto. AMBIGUOUS: no codomain is stated - if the intended codomain is [1/3,1] the answer would be C.

question: Let \(f(x)=[x]\), where \([x]\) denotes the greatest integer contained in \(x\). Which one of the following is correct?

options.label: C
options.text: Domain of \(f(x)\) is set of real numbers and range of \(f(x)\) is set of integers

options.label: D
options.text: Both domain and range of \(f(x)\) are set of real numbers

working: [x] is not injective (f(1.2)=f(1.7)=1) and not surjective onto R; the true statement is that its domain is R and its range is Z.

question: \(n(A)=8\), total number of bijections defined on \(A\) is
working: Bijections on a set of 8 elements = permutations = 8!.

question: If \(n(A)=4\) and \(n(B)=6\). The number of one to one functions from \(A\) to \(B\) is
working: Injections from a 4-set into a 6-set = 6*5*4*3 = 360 = 6P4.

The period of the function \(f(x) = \tan(4x - 1)\) is
working: tan has period pi, so tan(4x-1) has period pi/4.

question: Period of \(\sin\theta - \sqrt{3}\cos\theta\) is
working: sin(t)-sqrt3 cos(t) = 2 sin(t - pi/3), a single sine of argument t, so the period is 2pi.

question: If \(z_1, z_2, \ldots, z_{n-1}\) are the \(n\)th roots of unity, then \((1-z_1)(1-z_2)\cdots(1-z_{n-1}) =\)
working: x^n-1=(x-1)prod(x-z_k) gives prod(x-z_k)=1+x+...+x^(n-1); at x=1 this equals n. Numeric: n=3,5,7 gave products 3,5,7.

question: \(\lim_{x \to \infty} x \sin\left(\dfrac{2}{x}\right)\) is equal to
working: x sin(2/x) = 2 * sin(2/x)/(2/x) -> 2*1 = 2; numeric at x=1e9 gives 2.0.

question: If \(f\) be a function such that \(f(9) = 9\) and \(f'(9) = 3\), then \(\lim_{x \to 9} \dfrac{\sqrt{f(x)} - 3}{\sqrt{x} - 3}\) is equal to
If \(\lim_{x \to \infty} \left(1 + \dfrac{\lambda}{x} + \dfrac{\mu}{x^2}\right)^{2x} = e^2\), then
working: (1+L/x+M/x^2)^(2x) -> e^(2L), so 2L=2 gives L=1 with M unrestricted; numeric at x=1e7 with M=0,5,-3 all gave 7.38906 = e^2.

question: The function \(f(x) = [x]\) where \([x]\) is the greatest integer function is continuous at
working: [x] is discontinuous exactly at integers (1, 2, 4 all fail); 1.5 is not an integer so it is continuous there.

question: If \(f(x)\) is an even function, then \(f'(x)\) is

options.label: D
options.text: may be even or may be odd

working: Differentiating f(-x)=f(x) gives -f'(-x)=f'(x), i.e. f'(-x)=-f'(x), so f' is odd.
